source.title: تأمین کامل برق صنایع تا ۲۰ اردیبهشت
قطع برق واحدهای تولیدی به دلیل «هزینه ترانزیت»؛ ضرورت تدوین برنامه دولت در شرایط بحران
کمبود مواد اولیه، صنایع فارس را به فعالیت خاموش و روشن کشاند/ ۱۱۴۷ کارگر کارخانه لاستیک دنا در بلاتکلیفی/ رد بیمه بیکاری کارگران و تأکید بر بازگشت به کار
اشتغال حدود ۲۵۰ کارگر در فولاد سیادن/ امیدواری کارگران به بهبود وضعیت

claim.statement: On 29 April 2026, Iran Online reported Deputy Energy Minister Mostafa Rajabi Mashhadi saying industrial electricity-management restrictions, which began on 15 Farvardin last year, would be delayed this year and industries could use full electricity until 20 Ordibehesht 1405 (10 May 2026); after that, continuation would be decided weekly based on temperature, consumption, and production conditions, while industries with damaged dedicated power plants were asked to repair and rebuild.
claim.subject: Iran Energy Ministry

evidence.summary: Iran Online quoted the deputy energy minister on full industrial electricity until 20 Ordibehesht, weekly decisions afterward, and damaged dedicated power plants needing repair.

information_depth.rationale: Official statement gives a date, comparison to last year, decision rule, and damaged-plant caveat.

assessment.uncertainty: The statement promises delayed restrictions but does not prove actual industrial delivery after 20 Ordibehesht.

claim.statement: On 25 April 2026, Jamaran/Vista reported that several production-unit managers complained provincial electricity companies had cut their power despite payment for consumed electricity because separate 'transit' fees were unpaid; one producer said wartime conditions had effectively stopped production and destroyed liquidity, yet the unit was told to pay weekly or accept lump-sum/installment terms.
claim.subject: Iranian production units
claim.object: electricity cutoffs tied to unpaid transit fees amid wartime liquidity collapse

evidence.summary: Jamaran/Vista reported several producer complaints and quoted a producer saying production had effectively stopped under wartime conditions while transit-fee payment pressure continued.

information_depth.rationale: The report gives mechanism and producer quote, but not names, locations, or a count of affected units.

assessment.uncertainty: Need direct original Jamaran page or named firms to quantify the spread of this cutoff mechanism.

claim.statement: On 22 April 2026, ILNA quoted Bahram Zanoobi Tabar, head of the Fars Province Supreme Labor Council, saying raw-material shortages had forced some Fars industrial units into stop-start operation, with war conditions and damage to petrochemical and steel mother industries disrupting the supply chain; he said Dena Tire had about 1,147 workers, a proposal to put about 1,100 on unemployment insurance was rejected, workers were told to return, and layoffs had become a national challenge.
claim.subject: Fars Province industrial workers
claim.object: stop-start production, rejected unemployment insurance, and layoff risk

evidence.summary: ILNA quoted the Fars labor-council head on raw-material shortages, war and mother-industry damage, 1,147 Dena workers, rejected unemployment insurance for about 1,100, and layoffs becoming a national challenge.

information_depth.rationale: Named labor official, specific factory, worker count, insurance decision, and supply-chain mechanism are reported.

claim.statement: On 23 April 2026, ILNA quoted Siaden Abhar steel workers saying about 250 contract workers remained employed but were owed Esfand 1404 and Farvardin 1405 wages, while about 15 reinstated workers were still owed Bahman wages; workers said last year's electricity-cut problem had caused several temporary shutdowns, production had restarted and accelerated from Farvardin, and their priorities were current monthly wages and preserving employment through higher production.
claim.subject: Siaden Abhar steel workers
claim.object: wage arrears and reliance on resumed production after prior electricity-driven shutdowns

evidence.summary: ILNA quoted workers on 250 contract jobs, Esfand/Farvardin arrears, 15 reinstated workers still owed Bahman pay, prior electricity-cut shutdowns, and production restarted from Farvardin.

information_depth.rationale: Direct worker quotes give workforce size, wage months owed, and the current employment-preservation concern.

question.text: After 20 Ordibehesht 1405 (10 May 2026), do industrial power restrictions actually return, and do debt/transit-fee cutoffs create hidden shutdowns even if official rationing is delayed?
question.resolution_criteria: Post-10-May industrial power schedules; factory-level reports of outages; official notices from provincial power companies; worker reports of shutdowns or wage delays tied to electricity.
question.why_it_matters: Industrial electricity is a direct bridge between wartime infrastructure damage, unemployment, wage arrears, goods scarcity, and the regime's promise to avoid layoffs.

operations.rationale: Official delayed electricity restrictions and damaged dedicated power plants provide current context for factory shutdown and layoff pressure.
Fee/debt-related cutoffs show a second mechanism of industrial power loss even while official rationing is delayed.
Dena's rejected unemployment-insurance path and stop-start production corroborate wider post-war worker unemployment and weak safety-net pressure.
The Dena case shows the practical labor risk beneath Mojtaba's official call to avoid layoffs and support workers.
Siaden Abhar adds a factory-level wage-arrears and employment-preservation case to the broader unemployment/health-risk worker picture.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v10 — industrial power becomes employment pressure
synthesis.summary: The tenth pass adds an industrial-energy layer to the worker survival map. Officially, the Energy Ministry is delaying industrial electricity restrictions: Iran Online quoted the deputy energy minister saying industries can use full power until 20 Ordibehesht, after which continuation will be decided weekly, while factories with damaged dedicated power plants must repair/rebuild. But producer-side reporting already shows fragility beneath that promise: Jamaran/Vista says some production units have had power cut over unpaid 'transit' fees even after paying consumption charges, with one producer saying wartime conditions mean there is effectively no production or liquidity. ILNA then shows how this converts into labor exposure: in Fars, raw-material shortages tied to war damage and supply-chain disruption have pushed units into stop-start operation; Dena Tire's roughly 1,147 workers faced a rejected unemployment-insurance path for about 1,100 workers and were told to return. At Siaden Abhar steel, about 250 contract workers are still owed Esfand/Farvardin wages and are trying to preserve jobs through production after previous electricity-driven shutdowns. Net: Mojtaba's May Day appeal to avoid layoffs is colliding with power allocation, debt/fee enforcement, raw-material chokepoints, and wage arrears.
synthesis.limitations: Water-pressure results in this pass mostly duplicated existing Tehran-water rows and were not promoted. The transit-fee cutoff report lacks named firms or locations. The official industrial-power promise must be checked after 20 Ordibehesht with actual factory schedules, worker reports, and provincial power notices.

information_depth.rationale: The pass combines official energy timing, producer complaints, named labor-official reporting, and direct factory-worker reporting.

operations.reason: v10 adds industrial electricity allocation, power/debt cutoff, raw-material stop-start operation, and factory-level wage/layoff exposure to v9's Mojtaba labor-war narrative.
